Maintenance Report — MNT-0119-003

Asset: WELL-0119 (NE-07 Well 119, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: rod string Work started: 01 Apr 2023 08:00 · Finished: 19 Apr 2023 15:00 · Well stopped for this job: 439 hours Crew lead: Kevin Price (U-303) · Crew: Megan Ward Triggered by: inspection INS-0119-0023 on 2023-03-30 Report written: 21 Apr 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0119-0023 showed the wellhead at 19.9 °C with the air at 19.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 16 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rod string and located the break.
  3. Recovered the lower section with an overshot fishing tool.
  4. Replaced the damaged rods.
  5. Ran the rod string back in and spaced out the pump.

Summary of the fix: fished and replaced parted rod section.

Testing and return to service

Pump test showed normal fluid delivery and the rod load returned to normal. The well was returned to production.

maintenance.action: Replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil
maintenance.report_html:
Maintenance Report — MNT-0119-007

Asset: WELL-0119 (NE-07 Well 119, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: flowline Work started: 25 Aug 2023 08:00 · Finished: 25 Aug 2023 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0119-0043 on 2023-08-24 Report written: 26 Aug 2023

What happened

The weekly manual inspection INS-0119-0043 at 14:30 on 2023-08-24 found crude oil on the pad: about 8.2% of the pad area, estimated 2.5 bbl. The inspector noted: "Staining along flowline route." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.1 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a corrosion hole along the flowline route.

Root cause

External corrosion where the pipe coating had been damaged.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 2% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the leak point.
  2. Cut out the corroded section.
  3. Welded in new line pipe.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 188 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 150 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.9 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0119-007 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.8% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Parts and cost

ItemUSD
Line pipe and fittings3,311
Absorbents and berms1,471
Soil hauling and disposal2,575
Labour (company crew)3,284
Total10,641

Compliance check

ProtocolResultDetail

WS-02MetEnergy isolated and tagged
WS-03MetMonitors bump-tested; highest 0 ppm
WS-04MetPermit issued; gas test 2% LEL
WS-05MetTested at 1.25 × maximum operating pressure, held 4 hours
WS-06MetOily waste manifested to an approved site
WS-07MetWritten 1 day after the work (limit 3 days)

Notes and recommendations

  • Inspect the remaining joints on this flowline.
  • Record the leak location for the flowline maintenance program (RC-05).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0119-027

Asset: WELL-0119 (NE-07 Well 119, T200, Northeast Block 7) Equipment: downhole pump Work started: 14 Aug 2026 08:00 · Finished: 08 Sep 2026 11:00 · Well stopped for this job: 603 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman, Kevin Price · Contractor: Sandstone Rod & Pump Triggered by: inspection INS-0119-0197 on 2026-08-13 Report written: 09 Sep 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that fluid stopped reaching the flowline and the rod load spiked on the downstroke. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0119-0197 showed the wellhead at 41.6 °C with the air at 36.4 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The downhole pump was stuck, most likely from sand or scale. Sandstone Rod & Pump's workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 23 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

Root cause

Sand and scale build-up in the pump barrel.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 3 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Rigged up the company workover rig on the well.
  2. Pulled the rods and the insert pump.
  3. Inspected the pump: sand in the barrel and a worn plunger.
  4. Ran in a new insert pump.
  5. Re-spaced the pump and hung the rods back on.

Summary of the fix: pulled and replaced downhole pump.

Testing and return to service

Pump test confirmed fluid to surface and the wellhead warmed back to normal. The well was returned to production.
